title: Fastest recorded tennis serves

This article lists the fastest record serve speeds for men's and women's professional tennis. Max reported speeds are dubious due to the occasional errors with ATP radar equipment, especially speeds that have not been recorded twice by the same server, including all serves over 152 mph.

This list is not historically complete. For instance, not listed here, [Roscoe Tanner](Roscoe_Tanner "Roscoe Tanner")'s serve was clocked at 153 mph at Palm Springs in 1978 during the final against [Raúl Ramírez](Ra%C3%BAl_Ram%C3%ADrez "Raúl Ramírez"). There are also reports that [Bill Tilden](Bill_Tilden "Bill Tilden") had a serve that was clocked at 163.3 mph but there is nothing to verify that.[[1]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-bleacherreport.com-1) Also, [Ellsworth Vines](Ellsworth_Vines "Ellsworth Vines") in the [Wimbledon](Wimbledon_Championships "Wimbledon Championships") finals of 1932 clocked 121 mph (without Radar).[[2]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-2) Udayachand Shetty's winning serve was clocked by radar at 120 mph using a wooden racquet, at the Gilbey Gins fast serve contest held in Chicago on 24 July 1976.[[3]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-3) This qualified him to take part in the finals at the [West Side Tennis Club](West_Side_Tennis_Club "West Side Tennis Club") in [Forest Hills Queens](Forest_Hills%2C_Queens "Forest Hills, Queens") on 20 August 1976. [Colin Dibley](Colin_Dibley "Colin Dibley") of Australia won the event with a serve of 130 mph.[[4]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-4)

Currently, the Association of Tennis Professionals ([ATP](Association_of_Tennis_Professionals "Association of Tennis Professionals")) does not formally recognize service speed records made in [Challenger](ATP_Challenger_Tour "ATP Challenger Tour") tour events due to lack of uniformity in these tournaments' radar guns (including availability or lack thereof). Nevertheless, the serve speed of 263 km/h (163.4 mph) recorded by Australian [Sam Groth](Sam_Groth "Sam Groth") at an ATP Challenger event in Busan, South Korea in May 2012 was measured using ATP-approved equipment and other data gathered appeared within a normal range. However, [John Isner](John_Isner "John Isner") holds the ATP's *official* record for the fastest serve at 253 km/h (157.2 mph).[[5]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-5) Groth has more serves over 145 mph, having serves recorded at 146–147 mph at least 5 times at Grand Slam tournaments.[[6]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-6) At 20 years old, the american Ben Shelton served at 149 mph during the 1/8 finals of the 2023 US Open (he defeated the world no.14 Tommy Paul 6-4/6-3/4-6/6-4)

[Reilly Opelka](Reilly_Opelka "Reilly Opelka") with a 233 km/h (144.8 mph) second serve in the quarterfinals of the [2021 Italian Open](2021_Italian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2021 Italian Open – Men's singles") in Rome, holds the record for the fastest second serve ever recorded.[[7]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-7)

Multiple suspected issues in speed gun readings have been observed on ATP equipment. These include the recorded serves of [John Isner](John_Isner "John Isner") at 4,718 km/h (2,931.6 mph),[[8]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-8) [João Sousa](Jo%C3%A3o_Sousa "João Sousa") at 2,077 km/h (1,290.6 mph),[[9]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-9) [Denis Shapovalov](Denis_Shapovalov "Denis Shapovalov") at 424 km/h (263.5 mph),[[10]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-10) [Laslo Djere](Laslo_Djere "Laslo Djere") at 305 km/h (189.5 mph),[[11]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-11) [Alejandro Davidovich Fokina](Alejandro_Davidovich_Fokina "Alejandro Davidovich Fokina") at 252 km/h (156.6 mph),[[12]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-12) [Ryan Harrison](Ryan_Harrison "Ryan Harrison") at 244.6 km/h (152.0 mph),[[13]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-13) [Gaël Monfils](Ga%C3%ABl_Monfils "Gaël Monfils") at 242.0 km/h (150 mph),[[14]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-auto-14) and [Rafael Nadal](Rafael_Nadal "Rafael Nadal") at 230.0 km/h (142.9 mph).[[15]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-15)

Criteria to be listed in this article

- Men's serves must be recorded at or over 230 km/h (142.9 mph) minimum standard speed.
- Women's serves must be recorded at or over 200 km/h (124.3 mph) minimum standard speed.[[16]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-16)
- Only one serve per player is recorded here. For example, Andy Roddick has several 140 mph (225.3 km/h) or faster serves on his record but only his personal best of 249 km/h (155 mph) is included.[[17]](Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves#cite_note-17)
- In cases where more than one serve has been recorded at the same speed, the oldest recorded serve is listed first.
